data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for the procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services.
policy_statements.target: procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: This DR replaces DR 3300-1-A, Long Distance and International Telephone Service, dated March 23, 1999, and DR 3300-001-L, Local Telecommunications Services, dated March 23, 1999.
cross_references: DR 3300-1-A, Long Distance and International Telephone Service, dated March 23, 1999
DR 3300-001-L, Local Telecommunications Services, dated March 23, 1999

policy_statements.source_text: This DR will be in effect until superseded or the expiration date.
conditions: until superseded or the expiration date

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this DR within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may supplement this DR when developing their internal guidance.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: when developing their internal guidance

policy_statements.source_text: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR are not allowed.
policy_statements.target: Modifications to the intent or purpose of this DR

policy_statements.source_text: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR, one copy of each supplement will be forwarded to the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC), Enterprise Network Services (ENS), Organizational Compliance & Controls Branch (OCCB) at SM.OCIO.ENS.Policy@usda.gov.
conditions: If Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices publish internal guidance that supplements this DR

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to telecommunications devices (e.g., cellular phones, landline phones) that are provisioned for use on a third-party network and any associated telecommunications services.
policy_statements.target: telecommunications devices (e.g., cellular phones, landline phones) that are provisioned for use on a third-party network and any associated telecommunications services
conditions: that are provisioned for use on a third-party network

policy_statements.source_text: This DR excludes USDA wireless devices (e.g., laptops) that use USDA wireless networks.
policy_statements.target: USDA wireless devices (e.g., laptops) that use USDA wireless networks
conditions: that use USDA wireless networks

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA

policy_statements.source_text: The procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services depends on and is derived from the rules and regulations promulgated by Congress and the Executive Office of the President.
policy_statements.target: procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) §§11101 et seq., transferred the authority for the procurement and management of information technology (IT) from the General Services Administration (GSA) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB).
cross_references: Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) §§11101 et seq.
policy_statements.target: authority for the procurement and management of information technology (IT)

policy_statements.source_text: While no longer having authority for procurement and management of IT, GSA retained responsibility for negotiating telecommunications devices and services contracts on behalf of the Federal Government.
policy_statements.actor_name: GSA
policy_statements.target: negotiating telecommunications devices and services contracts on behalf of the Federal Government

policy_statements.source_text: Through this authority, and directed by OMB, GSA provides cost-effective solutions to Federal Agencies for procuring telecommunications devices and services from GSA contracts.
policy_statements.actor_name: GSA

policy_statements.source_text: OMB directs all Federal Agency Chief Information Officers (CIO) to review cost-benefit analyses, National Security System (NSS) requirements, and other substantive data when considering agency requests to use a vehicle other than the enterprise contracts for telecommunications devices and services.
policy_statements.actor_name: OMB
policy_statements.target: all Federal Agency Chief Information Officers (CIO)
conditions: when considering agency requests to use a vehicle other than the enterprise contracts for telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: GSA provides the contracting vehicles that support the landline and cellular telecommunications requirements of the Federal Government.
policy_statements.actor_name: GSA
policy_statements.target: contracting vehicles that support the landline and cellular telecommunications requirements of the Federal Government

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are directed to purchase telecommunications devices and services through the GSA enterprise and regional contracting vehicles unless the USDA CIO approves the use of an alternative telecommunications contract.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: unless the USDA CIO approves the use of an alternative telecommunications contract

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will determine their telecommunications requirements prior to procuring telecommunications devices and services to ensure the purchase of the appropriate number and types of telecommunications resources.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: prior to procuring telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure that new or existing telecommunications devices and services are aligned in accordance with the USDA Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework (IITGF).
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: new or existing telecommunications devices and services
cross_references: USDA Integrated Information Technology Governance Framework (IITGF)

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will maintain a comprehensive inventory of telecommunications devices and services, which is reviewed and revalidated at least every 6 months.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
policy_statements.target: comprehensive inventory of telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: When devices and services are determined to no longer be needed in current configurations, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will reallocate them for other approved uses, discontinue services, or dispose of devices through established procedures.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: When devices and services are determined to no longer be needed in current configurations

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will ensure that telecommunications devices, services, and facilities are fully compliant with DR 4030-001, Section 508 Program, and accessible to hearing-, speech-, and physically-impaired individuals.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Represent the USDA to the Federal CIO Council, GSA, and OMB regarding requests for exceptions to mandatory telecommunications services contracts;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Represent the USDA to oversight agencies, such as OMB, Government Accountability Office (GAO), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Department of Commerce (DOC), and Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on telecommunications-related issues;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Respond to oversight agencies with timely and accurate USDA telecommunications program and cost information;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the USDA liaison with international, inter- and intra-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA and intraLATA) telecommunications service providers;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO
policy_statements.target: international, inter- and intra-Local Access and Transport Area (interLATA and intraLATA) telecommunications service providers

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the USDA representative to the Diplomatic Telecommunications Service Program Office (DTSPO); and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO

policy_statements.source_text: Perform management and oversight responsibilities in accordance with the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291, as applicable to this directive.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291
conditions: as applicable to this directive

policy_statements.source_text: The ENS Director will:
Establish procedures for monitoring, measuring, and enforcing compliance with this DR;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: procedures for monitoring, measuring, and enforcing compliance with this DR

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with USDA telecommunications policies and procedures;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office compliance with USDA telecommunications policies and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Manage USDA telecommunications services, devices, and facilities in accordance with prescribed laws, regulations, standards, and related USDA 3300 Series telecommunications management directives;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: USDA telecommunications services, devices, and facilities

policy_statements.source_text: Review and render decisions for Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy waiver requests

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain an electronic file of approved waivers;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director

policy_statements.source_text: Work with Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to eliminate redundant or unused services and devices;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Include telecommunications requirements and initiatives as part of the telecommunications planning process;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director

policy_statements.source_text: Use GSA- and USDA-mandated programs when Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements can be met cost-effectively; and
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
conditions: when Mission Area, agency, and staff office requirements can be met cost-effectively

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain inventories of USDA telecommunications resources to the extent necessary to:
Ensure adequate and appropriate telecommunications resources to support Mission Area, agency, and staff office missions;
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: adequate and appropriate telecommunications resources to support Mission Area, agency, and staff office missions

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure accountability for USDA telecommunications property; and
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director

policy_statements.source_text: Meet Departmental and governmental requests for periodic or special inventory reports.
policy_statements.actor_name: ENS Director
policy_statements.target: Departmental and governmental requests for periodic or special inventory reports

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors will:
Ensure Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel comply with this directive;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure Mission Area, agency, and staff office internal directives conform to this DR’s stated requirements;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
policy_statements.target: Mission Area, agency, and staff office internal directives

policy_statements.source_text: Provide guidance to end users on the appropriate and secure use of Government systems-interfacing telecommunications devices;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Determine their telecommunications requirements prior to procuring telecommunications devices and services to ensure the purchase of the appropriate number and types of telecommunications resources;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
conditions: prior to procuring telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that new or existing telecommunications devices and services are aligned in accordance with the USDA IITGF;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
policy_statements.target: new or existing telecommunications devices and services

policy_statements.source_text: Use enterprise telecommunications contracts for Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) telecommunications services;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
policy_statements.target: enterprise telecommunications contracts for Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) telecommunications services

policy_statements.source_text: Establish controls for the strict management and oversight of all non-standard options in telecommunications services contracts for which the Government will be billed to avoid potential telecommunications fraud and abuse;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
conditions: for which the Government will be billed
policy_statements.target: controls for the strict management and oversight of all non-standard options in telecommunications services contracts

policy_statements.source_text: Appoint a Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer (TMACO) to select required telecommunications services from GSA program contracts for the agency or staff office.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: More information on this topic can be found in DR 3300-020, Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer Roles and Responsibilities;
cross_references: DR 3300-020, Telecommunications Mission Area Control Officer Roles and Responsibilities

policy_statements.source_text: Obtain waivers and approvals from the ENS Director when Mission Area, agency, and staff office telecommunications requirements cannot be met through mandated programs; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
conditions: when Mission Area, agency, and staff office telecommunications requirements cannot be met through mandated programs

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain inventories of USDA telecommunications resources to the extent necessary to:
Ensure adequate and appropriate telecommunications resources to support the agency and staff office mission;
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors
policy_statements.target: adequate and appropriate telecommunications resources to support the agency and staff office mission

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure accountability for USDA telecommunications property; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CIOs and Agency and Staff Office IT Directors

policy_statements.source_text: Meet Departmental and governmental requests for periodic or special inventory reports.

policy_statements.source_text: The roles and responsibilities for TMACOs are provided in DR 3300-020.

DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, Section 16, sets forth USDA’s policies, procedures, and standards on employee responsibilities and conduct relative to the use of computers and telecommunications equipment.
cross_references: DR 4070-735-001, Employee Responsibilities and Conduct, Section 16

policy_statements.source_text: DR 4070-735-001, Section 21, states that a violation of any of the responsibilities and conduct standards contained in this directive may be cause for disciplinary or adverse action; and

Such disciplinary or adverse action will be effected in accordance with applicable law and regulations such as the Code of Ethics for Government Employees, Office of Personnel Management (OPM) regulations, OMB regulations, and Standards of Conduct for Federal employees.
cross_references: Code of Ethics for Government Employees
Standards of Conduct for Federal employees

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices are required to conform to this policy.
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: If a specific policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated, Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices may submit a waiver request to the ENS Director for review and determination.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: If a specific policy requirement cannot be met as explicitly stated

policy_statements.source_text: Submit the waiver request to SM.OCIO.ENS.Policy@usda.gov.

The waiver request will explain the reason for the request, identify compensating controls and actions that meet the intent of the policy, and identify how the compensating controls and actions provide a similar or greater level of defense or compliance than the policy requirement.

Waivers to stipulations of this directive that have been granted approval by the ENS Director and that are associated with a control identified in National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, will be recorded and tracked as a Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) item in the USDA Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. §§3551 et seq., data management and reporting tool.
policy_statements.target: Waivers to stipulations of this directive
conditions: that have been granted approval by the ENS Director

Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), 44 U.S.C. §§3551 et seq.

extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy for the procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services.
extract_result.scope:
a. This DR applies to telecommunications devices (e.g., cellular phones, landline phones) that are provisioned for use on a third-party network and any associated telecommunications services.
b. This DR excludes USDA wireless devices (e.g., laptops) that use USDA wireless networks.
c. This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, contractors, data centers, cooperative partners, employees, and others working for, or on behalf of, USDA.

The procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services depends on and is derived from the rules and regulations promulgated by Congress and the Executive Office of the President.
procurement and management of USDA telecommunications devices and services

b. The *Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996*,  40 United States Code (U.S.C.) §§11101 *et seq.* , transferred the authority for the procurement and management of information technology (IT) from the General Services Administration (GSA) to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). While no longer having authority for procurement and management of IT, GSA retained responsibility for negotiating telecommunications devices and services contracts on behalf of the Federal Government. Through this authority, and directed by OMB, GSA provides cost-effective solutions to Federal Agencies for procuring telecommunications devices and services from GSA contracts.
